title: Fasten a spring-loaded access plate while maintaining its preload
instruction: Press the grey access plate level against its marked height while turning the eight orange nuts down their studs. Keep the plate controlled as the nuts capture its spring load. Seat every nut against the plate, then withdraw both hands; the plate must remain level and compressed.
context: A spring-loaded access plate can rise and tip until the threaded nuts capture its load. The expert transfers support between hands to reach both rows, turns and regrips every nut, and releases a level, compressed plate. This replaces an independent-nut repetition task.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; x forward, y left, z up; metres/kg/radians; XYZW quaternions. Tabletop z=0.7475 m. Fixed layout, seed 0, no object jitter. run_limit: 36000 control actions at 20 Hz (1800 simulated seconds maximum)
reset_notes: Native reset restores the authored layout and zero joint coordinates, settles through the official adapter, clears scorer history, and records a new episode. Native probes compare two reset repetitions within 3 mm. Seed 0; object_jitter=0.
fidelity: 4-mm-lead square threads use 16 rigid contact sectors per turn, 1.70-mm axial tooth thickness, 0.60-mm nominal axial backlash and 0.90-mm radial engagement. A vertical spring and two passive tilt joints model the access plate. Rigid-contact helix faces approximate manufactured thread flanks. Scoring measures pitch-coupled rotation and retained plate compression.
